WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW   What you already know
Chapters 2 and 3 treated direct labor as a variable cost with a constant rate per unit. That holds for mature products. Learning curves adjust the labor estimate for new ones.

EXAM TRAP   The rate is what remains, not what falls
An 80% learning curve does not cut time by 80%. After each doubling, the new average is 80% of the old average, a fall of 20%.

WATCH: NOT YET TESTABLE   The other model
Some texts use an incremental unit-time model, in which the time for the last unit falls by the rate at each doubling. It gives higher totals. The CMA LOS name the cumulative average-time model; use it unless a question says otherwise.

FALSE-FRIEND ALERT   Courbe d'expérience, منحنى الخبرة
French 'courbe d'expérience' and Arabic منحنى الخبرة usually mean the experience curve, which covers all costs across an industry. The learning curve here covers only labor time on one task.
